text:
Nice little joint, nice little waiter, nice little waitress If only this were what we eat out for it would be a five star review.

But we do have to consider the food do we not?

Tomato soup with basil, good flavour but to course in texture.

Meat loaf with mashed potato and mushroom gravy, Sounded good, was not good. I suspect the gravy was not made with a roux for thickening, but corn startch. It had the look and taste of a liquid clear plastic. If the potatos were real they found a batch that did a good job of playing the part of a boxed flake. The meat loaf had no discerning quality at all, so who knows if it was meat or tofu.

The iced tea was in a nice slender glass, but the flavour was of a nice tinted water. 

The cookie was very flavourful with a good amount of chips inside. 

So to say I enjoyed the food would be an untruth. Yes I will go back to try something else, just nothing with a sauce or gravy on it. 

I forgot I also got a side of beans. Again a very odd consistancy for the sauce in which they sat. Much too sugary with no other flavour.

In the film world, there's the "chick-flick."
In the lunch world, there's Arcadia Farms.
This place is the ultimate chick hangout, both young and old alike, offering great service, food, and ambiance, even valet parking. 
One small problem. 
If you're maie, and your testosterone level is fairly moderate, prepare to get sucked into a lunch vortex that could last for up to two hours. 
Not because of the service. The service is fast and very pleasant.
It's because when women get in this place, they don't want to leave. 

In my many experiences here, my wife has routinely drawn out what should be a 45 minute lunch into a seemingly endless afternoon of iced-tea refills and multiple trips to the mens room. 
This is when my testosterone kicks in, finding myself with the unpleasant task of sacking-up, demanding she not sample one more dessert, waving off the server and her next round of iced teas, and declaring it's time to go. 

Don't get me wrong.
I love good food in a charming atmosphere, but at some point, I feel like the Mad Hatter, Alice and the Red Queen are about to come bursting out of one of the rooms, validating my suspicions that Arcadia Farms is really one big tea party for chicks.
I will gladly return to this place, but only if I have an appointment scheduled for that afternoon which allows me to conveniently point at my watch while simultaneously raising one eyebrow, signaling its time to go.

This may work better than the 'sacking-up" scenario.

I've stayed here at least a dozen times over the past ten years, and the following comments would hold true for every one of my stays: If you're looking for a cheap place to crash in the heart of Hollywood with clean beds and bathrooms and absolutely nothing else (and I really mean nothing else), this is your best bet. The place is spartan and slightly shabby at best. The free wi-fi is perhaps the only perk. The front desk folks are usually worthless in terms of advice or suggestions and the rooms sometimes smell a bit funky. The motel's limited parking slots are assigned daily on a first-come basis and go quickly, so if you happen to arrive in the evening, you'll be forced to park your car at a lot located a block away.
So why stay here? Location, location, location (and price). You're walking distance from all of the major Hollywood attractions, as well as decent bars and restaurants, not to mention subway stations and bus routes. And you're within easy driving distance of the major movie studios and some great neighborhoods.

text:
My daughter and I stayed here while on Spring Break. We really appreciated how close it was to many of the major sites we wanted to see. It was nice having a microwave and fridge in the room for snacks and leftovers. Our view wasn't very scenic (a loading/parking area), but we weren't much bothered by it. Bus stops, subway, and bike rental were all within a block or so of the hotel. We had a complimentary breakfast buffet whose contents were predictable, yet tasty. Our waitstaff were unfailingly pleasant. The bar offered evening drink specials, which were also quite welcome!
One quibble: The evening we went down to use the pool, we found it small and unbearably chilly. Even my daughter (who must have inherited her "polar bear" genes from her father) thought it was too cold. I would think that even if the hotel caters primarily to business travelers, the pool would be bigger to accommodate lap swimmers. I hope its temperature that night was an unusual glitch.
If you go to Washington, do familiarize yourself with the local public transit system. I was very happy with their coverage, the frequency of their buses/trains, and surprisingly, their website. Their Trip Planner ( <url> is very helpful and right on the mark!
As mentioned in some of the other reviews here, they roll up the sidewalks in this area right around 6 p.m. As much as we liked this hotel, the next time we come (now that we're familiar with the Metro system), we'll probably try to find something around DuPont Circle.

text:
My foodie friend recommended this place to me when she found out I was going. She said it was like the best meal she ever had, and I completely agree with her. 

We made late reservations after a show, we got there earlier than expected but the staff was more than accommodating. They seated us way before our reservation time. The ambiance of the restaurant was so inviting, it would have been great for a large group of people celebrating and a more intimate date type situation. 

We chose to do the chef's menu. There were just way too many selection and this way was easier. For the chef's menu you choose from I think three types of meat, the angus beef, the domestic wagyu, and a surf and turf. The prices are set accordingly, 115, 140, and 160 respectively. Since everything is shared, you can't choose an option different from your table. (Maybe a bigger group can, but it was just me and my BF and we had to choose the same type of meat) We let the chef choose what cuts to give us and how to prepare, you can't go wrong there. They also gave us the option of choosing what sides we wanted, or just have the chef choose what he thought would go best with the main dishes. We let the chef choose and loved everything. The roasted red bell peppers with garlic was my favorite. The wagyu beef tartare was freakin amazing!! There was also a plate of various types of mushrooms, you'd love it if you're a mushroom fan. The potato puree was delicious, buttery and creamy. There was also grilled prawns, an arugala salad, and roasted corn....all were delish. Even the complimentary dinner rolls were awesome!!! They came in the baking dish they were made in and were sprinkled with sea salt. 

There was soooo much food, even big eaters like me and the BF had trouble finishing everything. The meal was worth every penny...so I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone who's celebrating in Vegas or just wants a great meal experience. The service was top notch, they made sure we were comfortable, understood the menu options, and made recommendations to us for drinks they thought we'd like.

My only complaint is their red sauce, I was glad the pizza didn't have a lot of it. I just wasn't a big fan, can't quite put my finger on why. But I'm weird with my sauce preferences. Prices are about on track with most quality pizza places.
Can't wait to go back, Looking forward to trying their white pizza and original cheesesteak which I'm hearing good things about.

text:
A group of us (9 forty-something friends) went to the Immerse Spa at the MGM Grand Detroit for the day, and we rented 2 rooms for that Saturday night. I have mixed feelings about the whole experience...
The day before our stay I received a call saying we'd be receiving a suite since the locker room was going to be crowded that day. That was a very nice bonus since we could have food/drink in the room (outside food is allowed poolside.)
The spa is gorgeous - we were here 2 years ago for the day (no hotel rooms) and loved it then too. The massages are outstanding, the pool area is gorgeous, even the hallways are beautiful and serene. Since we booked our spa services as a group, a limo ride was included with our package. But...the limo never showed up at our Detroit suburb location (30 min drive) and by the time I called to inquire about where it was, we were cutting it dangerously close to our spa appointments. We ended up driving 2 cars into the city (such a huge disappointment - half of the spa fun was the limo ride!!) They barely apologized for this, and as a "sorry for your troubles" gesture, they gave us 9 bottles of used nail polish in our room. ??? Yuck.
All in all though, a great day at the spa...despite being bummed about the limo. We mentioned our limo snafu at the front desk and asked them if we could get a limo ride to Mexican village for dinner - about a 10 min ride. So we were happy about that. However, the customer service wasn't anything to write home about. Nobody seemed overly concerned about this glaring lack of service.
When we returned from dinner at 11 pm, the otherwise calm & not-very-crowded casino/hotel lobby had turned into the biggest freak show I've ever seen. We apparently didn't get the memo to bring our spandex, sequins, and 3" skirts. The trashy women (young, old, beautiful, hideous) and their cleavage were everywhere...and at least half of the "clientele" (I use that term loosely) was absolutely wasted. Others in the casino: hillbillies wearing jeans and tshirts, elderly people with oxygen tanks/walkers at the slot machines, ganstas & hip hop thugs with their pants hanging, and most likely ladies of the evening. It was absolutely crazy town. Lots of bachelor parties, bachelorette parties, 21st birthdays, etc.
So we decided to sit in the hotel lobby for the next TWO hours people watching in the hotel lobby by the beautiful 100 ft long fireplace. It was the most I've laughed/cried in a long time. One guy ran right into a plant, someone fell on a couch near us, men were feeling girls up, people were weaving across the floor instead of walking, and I saw more stilettos than I've seen in my life. We had to wonder, how are these trashy people able to afford the rooms? You had to show a hotel card key to get into that particular lobby at that hour.
I'd describe it as Kardashian-trashy...Vegas wanna-bes. I'm no prude...we had drinks most of the day, but what we saw was beyond crazy. Highly recommend the Sat. night people watching if you want some good laugh therapy.
PS Oh yeah, the hotel rooms were gorgeous (and smoke-free). The casino itself is a giant ashtray. Stick to the hotel lobby for people-watching. :)

text:
Oh, Athenian Express. You were so promising, alluring, and tempting when I walked in the door and yet, so disappointing.

The bad:
- Awful gyro meat. This tastes like the gyro meat at Crave sandwiches, which we all know isn't real gyro meat. 
- THREE slices of gyro meat. THREE. I took a picture to prove that it literally only came with three slices. Whichever reviewer said that their sandwiches were bigger than a Kronos lied and lied mercilessly. Seriously, who gives three slices of meat?
- The sauce was mediocre. It's homemade, but that doesn't mean it has to be mediocre. 
- Fries aren't anything special. They taste like fries that come in a bag, no special seasoning or anything. 
- Cubs fans. Enough said. 

The good:
- I ordered fries, which I got, but they also gave me fruit. I don't know why, but this saved the review from being one star because the fruit salad had mango AND orange in addition to melons and strawberries.
- Fast service. Damn fast. Maybe too fast since they gave me so little meat.

Overall:
I was so excited to go here because I only get gyros on a special occasion. Well hot damn, I won't go back. I'm going to stick to George's Famous Gyros on McKellips in Tempe where not only are they not Cubs fans but they use real gyro meat.

text:
When I read the reviews about this Hilton Resort, I had some concerns. But, traveling with a small child I felt the available water activities and the 2-room suites would be best. If you are looking for a quiet and relaxing spa or adult weekend, this is not the hotel for you. If you are looking for great poolside service and fancy drinks with umbrellas, find another resort. As a Hilton Diamond Member, I am used to a level of service that this hotel does not offer. In fact, you will not receive anything special for being a loyal Hilton customer. So, Diamond members, do not look for a nice sit-down continental breakfast as it is not offered. Our two choices are to stand in line in the gift shop for dry cereal, and even drier donuts and coffee. Or, the other option is to pay for breakfast at the noisy and unorganized Rico's restaurant on-site. ROOMS: Our two-story king bed casita was very nice. It was clean and comfortable. I liked that we could park in covered parking right at the casita. The bed was comfortable and clean. The kitchenette, fridge, etc. were new and well-kept. Very nice room. Not five-star but nice.
SERVICE: Checking in, we were greeted and received well. Quick service to our room. The restaurants and poolside service was terrible. None of the staff seemed interested in helping. Too bad because the hotel misses out on a lot of revenue from bar/alcohol sales. RESTAURANTS: Food was mediocre but prices were okay. Again, service was slow both before and after ordering. THE RIVER RANCH: This, and the other pools, are the hotel's saving grace. Our two-year-old had a blast. She loved the lazy river and the waterfalls. The pools were beautiful. They seemed manicured and the surroundings were also nice. Very nice. One complaint I read was that hotel guests were reserving poolside chairs and not sitting in them. We also noticed this but is something you must deal with at a large resort. Overall the resort is just okay. It depends on what you want out of your stay. I give it a 3 or 3 1/2 stars mostly due to service.

text:
I didn't realize that Quiet Storm was a completely vegetarian restaurant until I noticed the word "seitan" printed after every meat item on the menu. Normally I'd find this annoying, as I'm an unabashed and unapologetic meat eater. That doesn't mean I don't love a good veggie dish, but fake meat masquerading as real meat is one of my pet peeves. If you're going to serve vegetarian food, don't try to pretend it's anything else.

That grievance having been aired, I ordered the Blackadilla, a quesadilla boasting no false meat items, but stuffed with black beans, basmati rice, sweet potatoes, pineapple and cheddar cheese. It was delicious and filling, and at $8 for the enormous quesadilla and a small house salad, a pretty good deal. 

The menu at Quiet Storm is large, with breakfast and lunch/dinner items as well as an array of cafe drinks and desserts. In spite of the prevalence of seitan and tofu, there are a number of dishes that I look forward to sampling upon return.

And I do plan to return. As those of you who have read my other Yelp reviews know, the atmosphere of public places is very important to me, and the atmosphere at Quiet Storm does not disappoint. It's got a retro cool '50s diner vibe and a more modern but equally cool soundtrack that entices customers to stick around. The wait staff encourages this practice, giving diners plenty of space to hang out long after they've finished eating.

The one downside of Quiet Storm is its location, floating among gas stations and abandoned houses in Garfield, an area sandwiched between the more pedestrian friendly neighborhoods of Bloomfield and East Liberty, but not quickly accessible from either. It has to be a pre-determined destination rather than a drop in for random passersby. But that might just be OK.

text:
We'll start at the beginning.

First, the process of making an appointment depends very heavily on if you have a preference on who you see. If you're looking for something that week, or the week after, you may not have a choice. If it's not REALLY emergency but isn't something you want to wait two weeks to have checked out, you're still probably better off there than at the Urgent Care only because they have your records and a lab.

Second, the ladies and gentlemen in the office who check you in are incredibly nice. I'll give them that. Crazy helpful inasmuch as they can be.

The doctors seem to listen to keywords. Lots of keywords. And for each flagged keyword you get a test. I LOVED how thorough they were. And they set up a follow up appointment for a few weeks out to go over any lab results.

So why did I give them the Two Star "Meh. I've experienced better"? If you want your lab results before that 2 week follow up, you've officially thrown a wrench into their well-oiled system. If you need an emergency refill a week or two before an appointment, huge wrench. If you want a referral... wrench. 

I'm not talking complicated stuff here either. I mean they have verified they received your labs back 3 days ago and your best shot at getting anyone to read them to you in the next week and a half is to go get a copy of them and then take them to the urgent care. 

Very well-oiled machine, but I never knew a business workflow could be modeled after the Hoffman's character in Rain Man. All is well as long as you stick to the schedule they set up for you, but anything changes the whole thing falls apart and you're left there with the whole office frantically looking for their maple syrup and toothpicks. 

You're a doctor's office, folks. I feel like "unplanned things" should be in your portfolio. 

I left a doctor's office after 7 years because I felt their office staff was exhausting and they were a decent drive from my house. My sister recommended these folks because they did not have that problem, I'll agree with her there. I ended up just going back to my old doctor, it was a good decision for me. Drive and all.

text:
The greatest hotel experience ever. From the moment you walk in off Park Avenue you know you have arrived somewhere special. The plush interiors the glorious reception all smack of Art Deco opulence. To know of all the stars that have graced this old dames makes you feel part of the experience, you can still sense their prescience as you stroll the corridors. The room is so original it it was a real treat to stay there, some say this place is tired looking, but I have to disagree, if they were to modernise this wonderful hotel the charm would be taken away. It is a place to soak in history and we loved it. The bed is a dream, every night I muttered I love you to the wonderful mattress and bedding. The little touches like the original lit light switches and your own front door bell all add to this perfect experience. Please keep this hotel as original as you can. Location wise, how good 2 blocks over from 5th Ave, just a block down to Grand Central, 10 mins from Rockerfeller, the same time to Central Park, times Square was 15 mins away. This hotel is not the cheapest in New York, but it was worth every cent! We shall return.
Long live The Waldorf Astoria.

text: INFERNO starts off with a fairly impressive for a TVM starscape effect . We`re also introduced to a scientist who`s called Heller . Don`t you get it ? Heller , Hell-er , Inferno . So I guess someone on the production had some intelligence . However it does become more and more obvious as the TVM progresses that intelligence has been discarded throughout the storyline in order to appeal to an American TVM audience The story itself is overwhelmed by subplots featuring umpteen stock TVM characters like the tough liberal schoolteacher who`s trying to save a home boy from a life of crime , the doctor who`s lost his medical licence etc . In fact the story concentrates far more on these characters than the approaching disaster that all the potential tension and drama the scenario might have had soon goes up in a puff of smoke , and being a TVM we just know that there won`t be a downbeat ending There is an onscreen problem I noticed and that is everytime there`s an explosion there`s a massive fireball which looks ridiculous not to mention physically impossible . Look at the scene where the national guard are in a fight with a gang . A soldier fires a grenade into a tower block and the whole building explodes in a fire ball . What a small greanade containing no more than a few ounces of high explosive can do that ! No it can`t . There`s also another scene of army engineers blowing up a dam with plastic explosive and the same fireball effect is seen . Can directors please note that high explosive is not the same as napalm Having said that I did find INFERNO highly watchable for a TVM and at no time did I find myself wanting to turn it off . It did have some potential and let me repeat the special effects are fairly good considering the budget and it`s not as bad a TVM as some people are making out

The only issue we had was on our last night when a group of teenagers in the room next to us were having a good time running in the halls, banging on doors, playing on the elevators, etc. After 3 phone calls and 2 visits to the front desk, they finally quieted down at 3 am. We were supposed to be comped for a one night stay but that has not happened yet so am afraid we need to call to follow-up. A bit dissapointed in that since my husband is a Hilton Honors member.

text:
Just returned from a 7-night stay at this hotel. Our room #302 was a suite with 2 beds, living room with dining area and a kitchen.
As stated by everyone else, it is very close to the Foggy Bottom Metro Stop -- we highly recommend taking the very efficient DC subway and leaving the driving to the the locals! On a quiet mostly residential street. The beds and pillows were really comfortable so sleep was good. walls seem fairly thin but our neighbors tended to go to bed early or were very quiet.
The place itself needs some work. Floors seem to slant, carpeting is old and fairly dirty (hard to tell due to weird carpet pattern). In our room the cabinet doors on the TV stand and armoir in the bedroom were literally falling off. The bathroom was tiny and not very well kept. The kitchen had a new fridge and a stove, oven and microwave and dishwasher but there were hardly any utensils/plates and no bowls or "extras" to make it easy to cook anything if you wanted to. TV Remote controls did not work well, one did not work at all.
When we got to our room, the dishwasher had been run sometime in the week or so before and the water did not drain out and the kitchen smelled. They came to fix it the next day while we were gone but when the dishwasher was run again, the same thing happened. They did get it fixed by the 3rd day of our stay.
Housekeeping was inconsistent. I am sure they came to our room each day because the beds were made and trash emptied but some days that seemed to be all they did. On three different occasions, they took dirty towels but did not leave any clean ones and I had to call and ask for some.
All in all we mostly used our room for breakfast and sleeping as we were gone all day playing tourist. We did rent an in-room movie one night when we were tired.
A few other details:
There is a 7-eleven 1/2 block away, a Safeway nearby in the Watergate complex and a Starbucks at the Foggy Bottom Metro Stop. We mostly ate at Union Station, Downtown and in Chinatown.
We tried to check out the rooftop pool. That area was closed as it is seasonal. Pool is very small but we had hoped to catch a view from up there.
We took Super Shuttle from and to the DCA airport but it would have been very easy to take the subway as it picks up right at the airport. If you are staying more than a few days, the week long subway pass is an easy to use deal -- $32 for 7 days of unlimited use.

text:
It's going to feel awkward standing in one doorway after another, feeling in the way of busy servers looking for somebody, anybody to tell you where to sit. You'll be tempted to tap someone speeding by with a tray in their hands to ask for a hostess in what feels like three big houses stitched together to make the restaurant that is La Petite Marche. 
Worry not weekend bruncher, they see you and they will get you tucked in at a table so you can have a long, leisurely brunch consisting of so many wonderful flavors - just for you. 
*If you can talk your way into the skylight room do it - great light and adds to the whole experience.

Lots of menus will be handed to you, look for the brunch menu. Order some crepes that come with (deep breath):
Eggs
bacon
ham
sausage
sauteed mushrooms
baguette
fresh fruit
maple syrup
coffee

No kidding. Sound like too much? Mais non. Just a little taste of everything on your plate. It's sooooo good.
Noise level can be a little high, it looks difficult to maneuver a stroller through and tables can be pretty close together.
The food is completely worth it. Bring a friend to catch up with and enjoy this hidden gem.

text:
I’m new to writing hotel reviews but I’m certainly not new to the major hotel chains and I’ve stayed in all of the various star and diamond levels including the edges at one and five. This was my first time staying at a Club Quarters though and I honestly didn’t know what to expect. To put it bluntly, I was pretty darn impressed, especially considering the excellent location and the great rate we got. It’s not super fancy but neither is it low-end and you're never more than a couple blocks from whatever station or bus stop you need to reach. It’s got everything you require included in the base rate while leaving all the typically useless bullet points out of your hotel bill. If you need to be pampered like a baby then this is not your hotel. But, if you just need a clean and well maintained room in a great location that's managed by an attentive staff this might be the hotel for you.
Central Loop has that style of service that’s polished and available as soon as you require it but otherwise out of your hair and out of your way. It’s as well tuned as any business hotel I’ve seen at this price and I felt like it mirrored my own sensibilities pretty closely. Honestly, if I managed a hotel I’d probably try to run it and price it a lot like this place. Again, it’s not overly fancy and certainly not a resort, but if you’re looking for an unpretentious business hotel that doesn’t try to be anything more than what it needs to be you’ve found the right place.
I did find a few negatives though. The shower took a while to get hot in the mornings, which didn’t bother me but it might bother some folks. Also, even though there were no stains or anything I felt the comforter was a little musty and could have used a run through the washer. I did see the cleaning staff taking the comforters away so it would seem they are in fact cleaned on some sort of schedule. Everything else inside the room seemed nice and clean with no smell even my sensitive nose could pick up. I suppose the outside of the exterior windows was a little dirty but that’s starting to get into nit-picky levels for a downtown business hotel. For the most part this hotel was hard to find fault with.
The only extra fee I had to pay was the late check-out fee, but this is clearly stated up-front in your room and is completely up to you. You can stick around until noon for no extra charge. In our case we checked out of one room and got a late check out on the other room so we could stll freshening up again before our flights. For that a single late fee was completely worth it. The hotel will hold your bags for free even if you decide to check-out before it’s time to head to the airport or train station. I never expected to be this happy with our choice but in the end everything went really well and I can see myself staying here again whenever I need to be in downtown Chicago on my own dime.

text: I live locally and occasionally take advantage of the Four Seasons when there is a conference in town to spend a night in town. The last opportunity was about 10 years ago and it doesn't appear that the rooms have undergone any significant upgrades or re-design since then. Within the last several years I stayed in the recently opened Four Seasons in Denver and it was crisp and modern and smart, but the Philadelphia version just appears a bit tired in the guest rooms. The entry way and common areas have more of an energy to them and not as run down-- still in keeping with the historical sense of Philadelphia-- but not the guest rooms. I had no complaints on the service-- everyone was friendly and helpful as one would expect of a Four Seasons. We had breakfast off the menu and it was very good, a nice selection and the service by Mr. Nunes was excellent. I would consider going back even when not staying there. For out of towners who can afford it, the location is not to be beat-- close to the art museum and downtown restaurants.

text: This was the beginning of it all! Granted, this is not Friends at its best, but this was the show's pilot, let's not forget and not a bad one at that. We're introduced to the gang and Central Perk, where our story begins. Even from this first episode we get a sign of the Ross-Rachel relationship that will come over the next ten years, when Ross says: 'I just want to be married again' and Rachel storms in with a wedding dress on... probably not intentional as at the time the writers were going for a Monica-Joey relationship but fits nicely now when looking back. Something else.. in this episode Rachel is introduced to Chandler as if the two have never met before but in later episodes, the so-called 'flashbacks' this is contradicted as the two have met on three previous occasions. Nevertheless, the point is this a fine start to a great show. This episode may not be the usual Friends as we are accustomed to them, with the cast still a bit inexperienced but over the next few episodes we see why the show came to be what it was! text:
We stay at SPG Hotels often, mostly Sheraton Brand Hotels and they have a good rewards program. We always enjoy comparing Sheraton Hotels, in many ways they are very similar but in many ways they are different. The Sheraton Boston is an average Sheraton and here is why...
Arrival: We arrived on Thursday afternoon to a busy check-in area. Most Sheraton Hotels have signs that designate the SPG Gold/Platinum Members check-in line, this Sheraton does not. They have a SPG desk but not a sign saying where to line up to check in. We went to the SPG desk area and we were greeted promptly. Tom who checked us in was friendly and gave us most of our room requests.
The room: We were given a South Tower Corner Room on the 28th Floor. This Sheraton Hotel Room was like most other Sheraton Hotels Room, except the bathroom which was small but still workable. The room itself was in need of renovation; It had a desk that had some severe water damage, old curtains and a flat screen tv with poor reception. The bathroom was not only small it was in need of a major renovation; old bathtub, walls were stained and overall just very outdated. On the plus side the bed in the room was comfortable and the room (a deluxe room) was large. The view from the room was ok, you could see a little section of the river, Prudential Center and some of the local area. The way the hotel was built with two towers makes the view a little less desirable. If you are in the South Tower and get a North facing room you will see the North Tower and if you get a North Tower Room facing South you will see the South Tower, both of these types rooms block your view to a point.
The Hotel: The location of the hotel is perfect. You have two malls, The Prudential Center and Copley Place, both average to small sized malls with mostly high end stores. There is a decent food court in the Prudential Center and some other sit down restaurants, such as the Cheesecake Factory, also in the Prudential Center. The location provides easy access to public transportation and if you enjoy walking is not too far from the Museum of Fine Arts and Fenway.
PARKING: Parking at the Sheraton can be VERY expensive, $44 for valet parking and $39 for self (no in/out access) at the Prudential Center. The parking garage under Prudential Center is managed by "Central Parking"...if you go to their website they have coupons you can print for discounted parking. We paid $25 for every 24 hours of parking. You still don't get in/out privileges but we did take the car out once a day to make sure we got the $25 rate. They also have discounts for their other garages in Boston. Also if you park in the Prudential Center Garage be aware it is a huge garage with limited signs. If you drive in from the Sheraton entrance you will see private reserved parking to the right but on the left there is "open" parking and further down on the right there is "open" parking. There are two ways to enter the Sheraton Hotel from the parking garage, first walk back towards the entrance of the garage and if you look to the left of the parking payment booths you will see a small entrance to the Sheraton. The second way is to take the escalator or elevator to the Prudential Center Mall area and walk through the mall where there is another connected entrance to the Sheraton Hotel. This can be confusing at first.
There is some security concerns at the Sheraton. We had them give our room to another guest on the second day we were there, an honest mistake that was corrected quickly. We were thankful we were in our room at the time or they would have had access to all of our belongings. Again the front desk employee, Tom, corrected the issue.
Also if you stay in the South Tower you have to use your room key card to access the elevator or wait for someone else to do so, not great security but better than nothing. The North Tower you do not need your room key card to access the elevator...I'm guessing because these elevators also service the conference rooms and the entrance to the Prudential Center. The concern is this elevator also has service to the parking garage. So someone could go from the parking garage to any North Tower room floor quite easily. This could pose a bit of a security issue to the hotel.
Overall the Sheraton Boston is an average Sheraton it lacks in some areas but the location and staff make up for most of those issues.

text:
I stayed at Crowne Plaza Phildelphia West for one night, July 19, 2012. There were a lot of flights cancelled at PHL that night, so I believe that the hotel was experiencing unexpected last-minute volume.
The room: The room was clean overall, and the bed was very comfortable. The room looked to have been updated fairly recently, but it seemed like a surface update. New furniture, new linens, etc., but the room itself seemed tired and out of date. For example, the closet had those mirrored doors. The bathroom was clean but also seemed outdated.
Service: Check-in went smoothly for me even though there were a lot of other customers waiting around. The staff was generally friendly. The stand-out employee was a lady named Allison, who went above and beyond to make sure my stay went smoothly. The concierge was also super friendly and kind. The biggest blip involved a room service order. I ordered room service right around 10:00 (to be fair, when room service was closing down and the hotel was swarmed with new guests), and was told that food would take about 45 minutes. I received my food after an hour and a half and two calls to the front desk, and, again, Allison rescued the evening by personally bringing the food to my room. The food itself was not great, but may have been better if I had received it sooner. I was told that my dinner would be on the hotel due to the delay, but I found the charge on my credit card later (doh!).
Location: I am not familiar with Philadelphia, but this location seemed a ways out of the city. The hotel was very conveniently close to a Target and many restaurants.
Other stuff: I had some trouble with the Wi-Fi password, but once I was given a new password, it worked great.
Overall, I might stay at this hotel again if I found a really affordable rate.

Next time I will be heading to Kalahari in Sandusky. A much larger resort, with nicer and cleaner rooms.

text:
I've seen this show 3x and taken friends each time. Living in Vegas i've seen A LOT of shows and this is my favorite as it is quite easily the best bang for your dollar, very reasonable. More importantly, Prince is one of those timeless musicians who is both talented and unique in so many ways. It really is a great tribute to his work and the work of Morris Day and the Time.

Like other reviewers mentioned, if you haven't seen Purple Rain, see the movie then go see the show!

One note is that the show is currently at The Westgate Hotel, formerly known as the LVH or Las Vegas Hilton. It's a little off the strip but if you're staying close to a monorail stop it's super easy as the LVH has it's own monorail stop. If you're local it's easily worth the short drive/cab ride.

The venue is fantastic. Much better than when they were at the D and/or the Planet Hollywood. It is tiered so everyone can see the stage well and it's small, no bad seats. The other venues were fine as well, but this one is superior.

Jason Tanner is awesome as Prince and the lead guitar is a great musician (apologies I don't remember his name). 

Morris Day and the Time come on and keep up easily with the energy of Tanner and his sets. I really enjoy seeing Kendrick Harmon as Jerome. The dancing and choreography and work put into the Morris Day set is obvious. Seeing the two bands interact with each other (Morris and Prince) is always humorous. 

I have now seen this show 3 times and I've never seen another show in Vegas more than once. I'm sure i'll go a 4th time at some point when some friends are in town again and want to see a great show.

If you live in Vegas or are visiting, do yourself a favor and SEE THIS SHOW! You will thank us :)

I LOVE Xtreme Sushi :]
Warm greetings are projected right as you walk in the door.

My friend and I went today for the AYCE lunch deal and it was $20 per person until 3PM. After that, it counts as dinner and I believe it is $25. AYCE excludes sashimi, haha.

We were seated immediately and decided that we were going to sit at the bar. Our server was great and every time we made eye contact and it looked like we were in need of something, she was there to help us. Our chef was very nice and he gave our orders out to us in a quick and timely manner. He tried to converse with us also and we had a few laughs together.

Now the food!

text: I love this area of Tribeca as i used to live nearby in the 1990's. This quirky hotel has a suitably downtown vibe; all the rooms are different with the decor carefully designed to appear to have been thrown together with inherited furniture etc and the employees all seem to be 20 something chaps , all effortlessly neat,stylish and meaning well ( but not all that experienced in the tricky business of running a great hotel.) There is a great , dimly lit pool with a japanese feel in the spa. My main problem with this slightly expensive wondrousness is that it uses the next door restuarant , locanda verde for its catering and it doesnt open till 8 am which is useless for business travellers. The staff offer to get coffee/ food before then but they either forget whos responsibility it was to get it from the restaurant or the restaurant forgets etc. also, the lounge tables arent suitable for eating drippy poached eggs from ( they are knee height) and it all seems a bit of a bother for the staff. Overall then, a fine place to explore downtown from as long as you are not an early riser and as long as you realize that there is no catering that is owned by the hotel onsite.

I have to say, I don't understand the rave reviews. I wanted to love this place. However, I can't get over the insanely bad service.

First- the good. I do LOVE the interior. The decor is great. The drink list- great. 

That is where the greatness ended. I went with several coworkers for a Thursday evening happy hour. The place was packed. This is usually a good sign! Our experience at the bar wasn't too bad. It took a while for drinks, but that is to be expected due to the crowd. The bartender was friendly, once he was able to circle back to us, our drinks were timely and well done. 

After an hour we moved to a table. By this time, the crowd had thinned. The waitress literally stopped by our table 3 times in two hours (I kept track). Service is key to any restaurant and it flat out sucks here. We were spending hundreds on drinks, appetizers, and dinner. Oh wait, we never got to actually order dinner because the waitress never checked back in after our appetizers. By the time we got appetizers they were cold (each flatbread, truffle fries, and others I can't recall). They may have been good, but cold fries aren't pleasant. 

What a missed opportunity. I can't stand when places go all out on decor and developing atmosphere/quality menu and skimp on service. 

I had colleagues there the same night in a separate party. It took 40 minutes for their drinks. 1 hour for appetizers. 1 hour and 5 minutes for dinner. The timing sounds off to you too? They won't be back. I may give it another shot. However, FIX YOUR SERVICE! It has repeatedly been raised in comments. I hope Ten Penny listens. We could use them, it is a great concept.

I shared 3 arepas with a friend- carne asada, chicken asada, and the cold chicken salad. There are menus in English and Spanish, and in English the asadas are called wood fire. I ordered these three because they were identified on the menu with a small icon, which meant they were chef recommended.

There was a short wait because this is not fast food where meals are prepared ahead of time and placed under a heat lamp. They appear to be made to order and you can taste the difference. The cost of the arepas were $5.00 to $5.50 and cheese ($.50) and avocado ($.99) are extra. I liked the beef the best. 

What struck me was the size of the arepas. They were larger than I thought and one was enough to satisfy me for lunch. I had 1.5 arepas and was stuffed. The breading used is gluten free and is not chewy. I would describe it more similar to the crunchy outside of a buttermilk biscuit. 

The cons were a very small parking lot and it isn't in a very safe area (right across from the Olympic Garden). But overall I recommend this place and I'll be back to try the empenadas, which I was told were home made.

text:
When it comes to Vincenzo's, I'm officially a bit of an addict. Funny enough, I've never set place in the actual shop - I order my food from them via Grubhub. So this review is purely for food and delivery service.

Why do I say I'm a bit of an addict? Because when it comes to pizza places, it's often really, really hard for me to find reasonably portioned pizzas. Seriously - if you set a pizza in front of me, I will eat most of, if not all, of it. And when even most small pizzas are pretty huge, this means that often I just have to forgo pizza delivery in favor of a smarter dinner option. But then there's Vincenzo's, which actually has an appetizer that is basically a small four-piece pizza with any toppings you pick. Yum! And the one I got was still fresh from the oven - it was a little circle of heaven.

Also, I LOVE the soups here. You have to like Wedding or Chicken Noodle when ordering through GrubHub, but hey, it works for me! And by the way: LOVE their cheesecake! I had a piece of Oreo cheesecake tonight that was really quite good. Not Cheesecake Factory good, sure, but sometimes, you just want a bit of chocolate, and boy does this place meet that requirement!

As for the people, from my experience they're really considerate. I may order through an app most of the time, but if there's a problem, the staff has no problem calling me right up to let me know and offer an alternative. They've always delivered about 30 minutes ahead of the projected time, too - talk about speedy!

Honestly, since I'm paying about $11 per order WITH a 15% tip to this place, I really can't complain. They're affordable, they're reasonable, and honestly, sometimes you just need a few basics: pizza, soup, sandwiches, cheesecake, whatever. Thanks for being my go-to for some pretty good basics, guys!

text:
I don't know how or why, but throughout my life I've been to a staggering amount of sushi restaurants in Montreal. Is it a skill? A talent? An obsession? No, yes, and most likely. But out of all the places I've been to - and I'm very sorry to say this - this Kanda location is the one I like the least.

I've been to a bunch of other Kandas, and those were all fine. This one, though. The last time I went, I saw they'd hiked up their prices. Which would have been fine. It's an all-you-can-eat sushi place; you can get your money's worth if you try hard enough. But sadly, I was left with no motivation to do so.

The food was fresh, I'll give them that; and the waiters were fine, nothing abysmal to mention on that front. But the quality of the food was vastly different than what I've seen from other similar restaurants, and from other Kanda locations. The sushi was lacklustre and dry; the sashimi were cut way too tiny to qualify; and the regular food just had an overall bland taste that I can't really describe. 

In a nutshell, it wasn't the greatest experience - even for a sushi buffet - and especially not with the price hike. I probably won't be coming back to this Kanda.

We stayed at the Club Quarters Hotel off Wall Street for 3 nights when my mum and I came to New York for a girlie weekend in May 2012. The hotel was fine - the room was clean and had everything you needed for a weekend break - en suite shower, wardrobe, desk, TV - really, when you're only in NYC for the weekend then you only need a room to lie your head!
Location wise it was ok - it's in down-town Manhattan so you do have to get on the subway for all your major sight seeing - but it is about a 2-3 minute walk from Fulton Street Subway which has services on many of the Subway lines. To us, it was worth paying a little less for a down-town location rather than paying premium prices of central Manhattan. It worked out at $600 for a double room for 3 nights.
We booked room only - you can add breakfast onto your room once you get there in the pub next door - we did this one morning it was $10 each for continental breakfast which was ok - average really - and other mornings we found a nice cafe round the corner which was much better value for money and had service with a smile!
So, that leads me onto my GRUMBLE of the trip - the staff at this hotel and RUDE! Really rude! I am a typical Brit who doesn't complain but I actually had to say something as we checked out of the hotel at how unfriendly the staff were at this hotel - not that the staff member we complained too was particularly bothered!
On arrival the lady who 'welcomed' us was unfriendly - she didn't tell us what room number we were in or floor we were on just handed us a piece of paper with information on. She didn't explain that we needed to use our room key in the lift and she didn't explain breakfast situation.
Generally all the desk staff were unfriendly - on our way in / out of the hotel no one stopped and said 'hello' or 'goodbye' - we were ignored! Also, one day i asked one of the girls at reception if she could help us work a bus route out for a trip and she said that 'we don't have buses in Manhattan' and was unhelpful.
So - in conclusion - average price, average location, clean, adequate room - rude miserable staff!

The Margherita was bomby as well, but come on.... PESTO. Best of all, it didn't break the bank whatsoever. Obviously, the bill would have been larger had we been imbibing, but for food and good times people watching (on the "patio"), I would definitely return... and I plan to.

One of the owners is a local artist so there are plenty of fun things to look at even if you aren't watching a D-Backs game.
I like the atmosphere at the Gilbert restaurant the best. The outdoor patio is great, but the artist/owner runs the Scottsdale location.

While the hotel location was perfect and the staff reasonably friendly, I was surprised by the condition of our room. Upon check in, we discovered that our room did not have the 2 beds we requested (even though reservation indicated 3 people and we paid the extra person charge). A call to the front desk told us that no rooms with 2 beds were available that night and we should have called ahead with the request, even though it was noted on the reservation form.
Overall, the quality of the room was terrible. The carpet was filthy, the room smelled musty, and was very dusty and humid, so much so that the bed sheets felt damp all night. There was mold growing on the ceiling and wall, which the front desk seemed surprised to learn about. It makes me wonder how thoroughly the housekeeping staff is checking and cleaning each room when they turn rooms over each day. The mold likely hadn't appeared over night. The bathroom door would not shut all the way and there was more mold in the bathroom. Given the reviews on Trip Advisor and the price paid, I expected much more. Unless the hotel undergoes a major renovation, I'd advise you to book elsewhere. Your money is better spent elsewhere.

text:
First ever experience with Indian food and definitely NOT a fan.

Exterior definitely looked like a house as their name calls for. A tad bit worn both interior and exterior. Furnitures were simply cafeteria like tables and you order at the counter paying upfront.

Their # 1 rave after hominy stew was a must try so I did so and for sure there will be a no second time. Blindfold me and I would've never been able to tell if this was homemade or out of a Progress/Campbells can. Stew definitely had sufficient ingredient but simply lacks flavor. Abundant amount of hominy in every spoon but does not suit my palate at all. Protein was tough and soup tasted run down. 

Fried bread reminds me of chinese donuts served for breakfast except a tad bit more doughy and is flattened to a circular shape. The bread itself is a great foundation for both entree and dessert if all ingredients were done right. I ordered a taco and a dessert (all utilizes fried bread) and was devasted with the ingredient used. The chocolate butter dessert was simply a cup full of butter poured over a cup of chocolate syrup. NOt to mention that the bread was already deep fried. Enough grease where a pack of oil absorbant sheet can't even save. Flavor was just like how it sounded. 

Taco itself was ground meat, refried bean, lettuce and cheese. Definitely tasted like something you can get at a taco bell/ Del Taco. No special marination nor seasoning done. 

I guess if i'm ever craving fried bread itself and if I"m by the area..which will never be..I'd probably pick one up and slap something on there myself. However it wasn't all that unique to me since Chinese cuisine carries close to identical "fried bread' they make.

Plentiful parking. Poor service since I was turned down for needing an extra set of utensils.

-Susan

text:
This was a nice little find off the strip. We came for the lunch buffet which was $10.99/person. 

BUFFET ITEMS:Vegetable korma, yellow daal, chana masala, vegetable samosa, sweet rice, basmati rice, vegetable pakora, chicken tandoori, chili chicken, chicken makhani, chicken curry, goat curry and the BEST part was that they had my favorite GULAB JAMUN!! 

The chicken curry was very flavorful, it had a great balance of creaminess and spices. It also contained big chunks of chicken which is what most people tend to skimp on (abundance of protein is always a plus in a buffet dish). I was surprised that they had goat curry (gamey stuff is not my cup of tea so this one I did not try). The gulab jamun were little balls of perfection. 

SERVICE: our server was very attentive and quick to refill our glass of water.

I subtracted a star b/c although the gulab was legit, they only had the gulab and rice pudding for dessert. There was no mango pudding or the carrot halwa the sweet carrot dessert, but I guess you can't have everything. I also wasn't a fan of their naan that they offered. A good naan has a little bit of crispiness and SOME flavor. This NAAN HAD NO FLAVOR whatsoever and was very thick and heavy. It was more of a PITA than a NAAN. 
 
For $10.99, I would come again.

text:
Probably the best wood smoker in this price range
The design of this smoker, being vertical instead of horizontal, works very well with the natural flow of smoke upwards from the firebox to the chimney. So far have made smoked ribs, pork tenderloin, chicken and pastrami. The thermometer in the door is of little use, found it to register about 50 degrees less than actual temperature. Luckily I tested this while seasoning the smoker, and didn't waste any meat finding out the hard way. Additional sealing is preferred for the main door, smoke rolls out from all directions without it. For the price, I'm thrilled with it. If a hurricane carried it off, I would buy another one. Be sure to spray the interior of the smoking vault with canola oil and run a fire for a few hours to season the interior; this will help protect against rust on the inside. And, spring for the cover when not in use.
